title: Unauthorized Registration
description: Homeowner (EE1) can register an account without proper authorization or verification, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the Home Hub's data.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the registration process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the registration process includes any verification or authorization steps.

title: Inappropriate Data Collection
description: Homeowner (EE1) may enroll cameras/sensors without explicit consent or a clear purpose, potentially collecting data beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: No explicit consent or purpose statement is provided for the enrollment process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the enrollment process includes any consent or purpose statement.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Home Hub (P1) may process data from the Homeowner (EE1) without proper authorization or oversight.
assumptions: No explicit authorization or oversight mechanism is described for the data processing.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the data processing includes any authorization or oversight.

title: Guest User Access Code Leakage
description: Guest User (EE2) enters a temporary access code at the Home Hub (P1). If the code is not encrypted or transmitted securely, it may be intercepted or logged, revealing the user's identity and intent to access the front door.
assumptions: The guest user's access code is not protected by encryption or secure transmission protocols.

title: Home Hub Data Leakage
description: The Home Hub (P1) may inadvertently leak information about the guest user's access code or the fact that the user is attempting to unlock the front door. This could include logging the code, storing it in a temporary file, or revealing the existence of the guest user in the system.
assumptions: The Home Hub processes the access code without appropriate security measures (e.g., encryption, secure storage, or logging).

title: Unauthorized Access to Home Hub
description: An unauthorized user or process could access the Home Hub (P1) and read sensitive motion/door/sensor data before it is written to the Local Event Log (DS1).

title: Data Exfiltration via Home Hub
description: An unauthorized user or process could exfiltrate sensitive motion/door/sensor data from the Home Hub (P1) to an external entity or another process.

title: Unauthorized Access to Local Event Log
description: An unauthorized user or process could access the Local Event Log (DS1) and read sensitive motion/door/sensor data.

title: Data Exfiltration via Local Event Log
description: An unauthorized user or process could exfiltrate sensitive motion/door/sensor data from the Local Event Log (DS1) to an external entity or another process.

title: Unauthorized Access to Uploaded Media
description: Process P1 (Home Hub) may expose camera clips to unauthorized users or entities without proper authorization checks.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the upload process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if authorization checks are implemented or if the process is fully secure.

title: Data Leakage to Untrusted Storage
description: Process P1 uploads recorded camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2), which may be accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: DS2 is a DataStore, and the mapping table indicates DataStore->Process interactions are valid, but security controls are not specified.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if DS2 implements encryption or access controls for the uploaded data.

title: Data Leakage from Storage
description: DataStore DS2 may expose camera clips to unauthorized users or entities without proper authorization checks.
assumptions: No explicit authorization mechanism is described for the retrieval process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if DS2 implements encryption or access controls for the retrieved data.

title: Data Disclosure: Home Hub Exposes Motion Alerts
description: The Home Hub (Process P1) forwards real-time motion alerts to the Mobile App Backend (Process P2). According to the mapping table, valid interactions include Process->Process. This flow represents an explicit disclosure of personal data (motion alerts) from a process to another process. If the motion alerts contain personal data, this constitutes a Data Disclosure threat (Dd) as it involves the transfer of personal data across a boundary.
assumptions: The motion alerts contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assumption made based on the flow description stating 'real-time motion alert' being forwarded. If the alert is generic system status rather than personal data, this threat may not apply.

title: Data Disclosure: Mobile App Backend Receives Motion Alerts
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process P2) receives real-time motion alerts from the Home Hub. This process acts as a recipient of personal data. If the alerts are personal data, the backend's role in receiving and potentially processing this data constitutes a Data Disclosure threat (Dd) as it involves the transfer of personal data across a boundary.
assumptions: The motion alerts contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assumption made based on the flow description stating 'real-time motion alert' being forwarded. If the alert is generic system status rather than personal data, this threat may not apply.

title: Unauthorized Access to Motion Data
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may expose motion-detected data to the homeowner (EE1) without proper authorization or encryption, potentially allowing the homeowner to access private health or movement information.
assumptions: The backend system is accessible to the homeowner's device.

title: Data Leakage to Unauthorized Source
description: The homeowner (EE1) may inadvertently or intentionally share their motion-detected notification with unauthorized parties, such as family members or third parties, violating privacy.
assumptions: The homeowner has access to the notification and the ability to share it.

title: Data Leakage
description: Mobile app backend (P2) shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor (EE3). This represents a potential data leakage risk where sensitive user data is transmitted externally.
assumptions: The backend process is configured to transmit all aggregated analytics data to the vendor without additional filtering or masking.

title: Data Leakage
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) may share aggregated device-usage analytics with the mobile app backend (P2). This represents a potential data leakage risk where vendor data is transmitted back to the internal system.
assumptions: The vendor's data export settings allow full transmission of analytics data to the backend process.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: The video clip stored in DataStore (DS2) is retained for a duration longer than necessary for the homeowner to play it back, constituting a violation of the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: The video is stored indefinitely or for an extended period beyond the functional requirement of playback.

title: Unauthorized access to video data
description: The mobile app backend (P2) has access to the video data stored in DS2, which may be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for purposes beyond the intended playback.
assumptions: The app backend is not configured with strict access controls or data minimization.
